newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols flat, eyes on 114 strike.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols flat, eyes on 114 strike.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were little changed as bond prices meandered in narrow ranges just below Wednesday's close, traders said.

They said Friday's June producer price index (PPI) was unlikely to pour cold water on the mildly bullish market and weekend time-decay was starting to weigh on option pricing after an uneventful week so far.
"Come eight o'lock tomorrow morning (just after 0730 CDT/1230 GMT release of PPI), it will be really dead," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for September T-bond futures options was just a touch easier at about 8.0 percent, while the soon-expiring August dipped a quarter point to around 7.0.
Traders said T-bond futures have had a tendency to gravitate toward an option strike price with high open interest concentration just prior to option expiration in the past several months.

That strike price this month, with August options expiring in a week on July 18, would be 114. September futures, which August options settle against, have hovered just below 114 after Monday's rally.
For July, June and May option expirations, 112, 110 and 108 respectively were the gravitational strike prices.
According to the CBOT, August 114 calls had open interest of 25,380 contracts at Wednesday's close, while 112, 113 and 115 calls had 15,737 lots, 23,306 and 12,568 respectively.
One firm was said to have bought 2,500 contracts of August 114 calls today, while another firm sold 1,000 lots of August 114 straddles.
A second CBOT trader noted that September futures soared away from the 112 strike immediately after the July expiration at noon on June 20.
He added, however, that open interest in August options was not very high on an absolute basis and the bond market could start moving again on upcoming economic data and events.

Traders said next Tuesday's June retail sales data might carry more weight than Friday's PPI or next Wednesday's consumer price index, given tame inflation figures in recent months. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony is also due soon on July 22, although this is after the August expiration.

In Eurodollar options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, implied volatilities were little changed amid moderate two-way trading. Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures option stood little changed at around 9.4 percent.

One firm was seen selling 1,000 contracts of June 94.00 straddles as well as 500 of 93.75 straddles in short-June contracts, which are options expiring in June 1998 but priced off June 1999 futures. On the other hand, a Wall Street firm was said buying 1,000 of the June 94.00 straddles.
"There's no pattern, pretty haphazard trading," one bank affiliate trader at the CME said.
